claims.claim: 'Formally verified' certifies code against a specification

claims.claim: Formal verification means proving or disproving, with mathematics, that a system is correct with respect to a formal specification or property

claims.claim: The specification is a precise statement of what the code must do, written in a logic a computer can read
A proof assistant, a program that checks proofs, examines each step mechanically, so a wrong step is rejected instead of skimmed over
Lean is the language DeepMind's agents wrote in

claims.claim: A test runs the code on chosen inputs and shows it behaves on those inputs; a proof covers every input the specification describes, which is how it can catch the rare case a test suite never tries

claims.passage: Validation: 'Are we trying to make the right thing?' ... Verification: 'Have we made what we were trying to make?'
